catalog.summary: Menu opened by right click on a target.

patternStatus: The APG has no context-menu pattern. The surface is the menu pattern's, held by specs/components/menu/contract.json; the four keys of the menu-button pattern are not taken on the target, because a region is not a button. The two keys that open a context menu from the keyboard — Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key — are a platform convention, named by docs/component-features.md §8, and shipped by none of the four surveyed libraries. Both pages were read on 2026-09-16 and the target's own keys are transcribed

roles.root: none. The target is a generic region the consumer wraps; the surface's roles are menu's.

holdsReason: The family is a target over the menu family rather than a second copy of it. Radix's ContextMenu re-exports the sixteen parts its DropdownMenu already has and its two documentation pages repeat each other nearly line for line; Ark adds one ContextTrigger to the menu it has, and the Angular CDK one directive. This family takes the second shape, as menubar did: a consumer imports MenuContent and its items from menu, and nothing is re-exported. The cost is one context, paid in menu once: the surface has to know its anchor is a point and where focus goes back, which are the two capabilities menu's own contract promised — a virtual anchor (inventory l. 117) and finalFocus (focus.finalFocus) — and had not shipped.
composesReason: Every overlay module reaches the family through menu. The family itself builds a PositionerAnchor — an object with getBoundingClientRect — and hands it to the menu; it imports the type and no module.
rootReason: menu and popover record that a trigger is not a part: a control that opens a surface is the consumer's own element and very often another family's root. A context target is not a control. It is a region — a row, a card, a canvas — that the consumer wraps, and the wrapper is the family's own element: Radix renders a span, Base UI a div, Ark a button it names context-trigger. The root renders a div and takes render for a row; a consumer rendering it onto another family's element keeps that element's identity, because the other family's props are spread after this one's.

contextmenu.effect: preventDefault while the family is enabled. While the surface is open the anchor moves to the new point and the surface repositions; no request is emitted, because open did not change.

longPress.effect: touch and pen only. data-pressed from pointerdown to release; movement past the threshold, pointerup or pointercancel before the delay cancels. A contextmenu the platform fires afterwards is prevented and moves nothing.

keyboard.effect: Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key, with focus on the target. The contextmenu event Windows fires for the key is prevented and ignored.

longPress.reason: Radix, Base UI, Ark and React Aria open a menu on a long press, and there is no secondary button on a coarse pointer. 500 ms is the value tooltip already holds as touchDelay; Ark uses roughly 700. The threshold is what tells a press from the start of a scroll.

primaryPress.reason: The target is registered as a branch of the layer, so the menu's own machinery treats a press on it as inside; the family says otherwise for the primary button alone, because the target is elsewhere from the reader's side.

closing.contextmenuInsideLayer: prevented, so the browser does not draw its own menu over the family's
closing.rest: escape, outsidePress, select, dismiss and programmatic are the menu's

keyboard.effect: opens the menu anchored to the target
opens the menu anchored to the target

keyboard.focus: the element that held focus when the menu opened, or the target

keyboard.effect: closes every surface and moves on
keyboard.focus: the next element in the page after the target

keyboardReason: Every key inside the surface is the menu's and is held by its contract. The menu-button pattern's four trigger keys — Enter, Space, ArrowDown, ArrowUp — are deliberately not bound on the target: a row uses them for itself.

focus.restore: the element that held focus when the menu opened, captured at that moment; the target when nothing did
focus.restoreMechanism: finalFocus on the menu, a ref the family writes at open
focus.tabindexReason: A target the consumer did not make focusable cannot be opened from the keyboard, and the reference page says so. A tabindex written here would add a tab stop to every wrapped region, which a grid with roving focus cannot afford; a row that is keyboard-reachable is already focusable.

wiring.data-open: on the root while the surface shows
wiring.data-pressed: on the root while a long press is running
wiring.data-disabled: on the root while the family lets the browser's own menu through
wiring.id: the menu's triggerId, so the surface is named by the target's text unless MenuContent is given aria-label
wiring.aria-haspopup: never written. It is not permitted on a generic element, none of the four surveyed implementations writes it, and a context menu is found by convention — which is why every action in it exists by another path as well.

naming.default: aria-labelledby the target, which the menu writes when its content has no aria-label
naming.reason: For a row or a card the target's text is the name of the thing the commands act on. For a canvas or a document the consumer gives MenuContent an aria-label, and the reference page shows both.

menuApi.reason: Items, groups, separators, submenus, checkbox and radio items, shortcuts, typeahead, loop, closeOnSelect, mount and the layer's positioning axes are menu's and are imported from it. Re-exporting them here would be Radix's shape, where two copies of one machine drift.

modal.reason: Radix defaults its context menu to modal and Base UI ships a Backdrop. menu declined modality for the reason docs/component-features.md §8 gives the modal surface to Dialog, and applyInert would inert the target itself.

alignOffset.reason: Base UI offsets a root context menu 2 px from the pointer. Windows and macOS put the surface's corner on the point; a gap between the pointer and the surface is a gap the pointer has to cross, and the first item is highlighted by movement rather than by arrival.

triggerKeys.reason: Enter, Space, ArrowDown and ArrowUp open a menu button and are not bound on the target: a region is not a button, and a row uses those keys for itself.

triggerAria.reason: aria-haspopup is not permitted on a generic element and would announce a popup a screen reader cannot reach by the announced means. The cost — a reader is not told the region has a menu — is paid by the rule that every action exists elsewhere.

stateModelReason: The menu's own model, surfaced by the family. ContextMenu in React renders the Menu and forwards open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange; in Angular the state is sl-menu [(open)] itself and the directive only asks it to move, so there is no second owner.
statesReason: The root paints nothing at rest, on hover or on focus: its content is the consumer's. open draws the mark Finder and Explorer leave on the row whose menu is showing; pressed turns off text selection and the iOS callout for the duration of a long press and nothing else; disabled says the browser's own menu is the one that will open.
